question.problem:
The function $f(x)=\frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{kx}+2$ has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}-5).
$$

What is the value of $k?$

current_example.problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac12 e^{x+8}-2.$
current_example.worked_solution:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x+8}-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{y+8}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{y+8}-2 \\ \frac{1}{2}{e}^{y+8} & =x+2 \\ {e}^{y+8} & =2x+4 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y+8}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+4) \\ y+8 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+4) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+4)-8\end{aligned}
$$

     

Therefore, the inverse function is $f^{-1}(x) = \ln{(2x+4)} - 8.$
